title: You don’t actually struggle with confusion—you struggle with authority.
paragraphs: You don’t actually struggle with confusion—you struggle with authority.

Because when the Bible says something that cuts across what you feel, what you want, or what someone else told you… you hesitate. You pause. You start searching for a softer interpretation, a more comfortable explanation, something that lets you keep control while still sounding spiritual.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
The moment you place your opinion above Scripture, you have already chosen a different authority. And it isn’t God.

You were sitting there, scrolling, listening, comparing voices. One preacher says this. Another says that. A friend tells you what “they think it means.” And somewhere in the noise, the sharp, unfiltered voice of God gets buried under layers of human reasoning.
God saw it.
You knew.
You knew the verse was clear… but clarity is uncomfortable when it confronts your life.
“For the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing to the division of soul and spirit…” (Hebrews 4:12)
Read that again.
Sharper. Piercing. Dividing.
That means Scripture was never meant to agree with you. It was meant to expose you.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.

There’s a quiet danger that creeps in when people start saying, “Well, that’s your interpretation.” It sounds humble. It sounds tolerant. But underneath it is rebellion dressed as wisdom. Because not every interpretation is valid when God has already spoken clearly.
“All Scripture is breathed out by God and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness” (2 Timothy 3:16).
Reproof. Correction.
Not suggestion. Not negotiation.
Correction.
You don’t correct God’s Word. God’s Word corrects you.

And this is where it gets uncomfortable… because you’ve done it before. You’ve read something in Scripture and immediately softened it. Adjusted it. Explained it away. Not because it was unclear—but because it demanded change.
You remember that moment.
The conviction hit. You felt it in your chest. That quiet, pressing weight that said, “This is about you.”
And instead of surrender, you reached for explanation.
But explanation cannot save you.
Only truth can.
“Knowing this first of all, that no prophecy of Scripture comes from someone’s own interpretation” (2 Peter 1:20).
Let that settle.
Scripture does not belong to human opinion. It does not bend to culture. It does not evolve with your preferences. It stands—unchanged, unmoved, unshaken.
“Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away” (Matthew 24:35).
So if God’s Word doesn’t move… then the real question is—why are you trying to?
There’s a breaking point here. You can feel it.
Because either Scripture is the final authority… or you are.
And you already know which one leads to life.
“Trust in the Lord with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding” (Proverbs 3:5).
Your understanding feels right sometimes. It feels logical. It feels compassionate. But feelings don’t carry authority—God does.
And here’s where everything shifts.
Because the Bible is not just a book of rules—it is the revelation of Jesus Christ.
“In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God” (John 1:1).
When you resist Scripture, you are not just resisting text—you are resisting Him.
Jesus doesn’t ask for partial agreement. He doesn’t ask for filtered obedience. He calls for surrender.
“If you love me, you will keep my commandments” (John 14:15).
Not reinterpret them.
Keep them.
And yet—this is where grace breaks through.
Because even after you’ve ignored, twisted, or avoided His Word… He still calls you back.
Not to shame you—but to save you.
“All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned—every one—to his own way; and the Lord has laid on him the iniquity of us all” (Isaiah 53:6).
Your opinions. Your detours. Your resistance.
All of it placed on Christ.
That’s the Gospel.
Not that you figured it out—but that Jesus paid for every moment you refused to listen.
And now you stand here, with a decision in front of you.
Will you continue shaping Scripture to fit your life?
Or will you finally let Scripture reshape you?
One leads to comfort that fades.
The other leads to transformation that lasts.
Say it plainly—“God, Your Word is final.”
Let that be your line.
